diagram_math_checks.objects: Unit sphere S^n in R^(n+1), its normal coordinates (p,t), and the open shell 1/2<||x||<3/2.
diagram_math_checks.check: The circles at drawing radii 1,2,3 represent geometric radii 1/2,1,3/2 in exactly the ratio 1:2:3. The even-odd fill leaves the inner disk empty; dashed inner/outer circles denote excluded boundary, matching the strict inequalities in Example lines 35–36 and step 2.1.

Step 1.1 identifies each normal vector with tp. In drawing coordinates p=(2,0), x=(2.65,0), so t=0.325 lies in (0,1/2); the rightward arrow has displacement (0.65,0)=tp at this scale. It is offset vertically only for readability. Its orientation and x label match step 2.1.

For nonzero shell x, x/||x|| is unit and ||x||-1 lies in (-1/2,1/2). Since 1+t>0, ||E(p,t)||=1+t, giving both inverse composites as identities, exactly as in step 2.1. Caption repeats this established inverse without introducing a new claim.

diagram_math_checks.scope: The circle is explicitly described as a schematic radial cross-section for S^n, not an assertion that every sphere is one-dimensional.
diagram_math_checks.check: Signed t<0 moves toward the origin and t>0 away because 1+t remains positive throughout the allowed interval. No commutative relation or new supplier is asserted.
